findings.claim: The Outcome's quiet-check paragraph states journal record 22 is 'the first use' of harness check --quiet with '1,272 bytes back to the caller', but record 22's own data has no output_omitted/output_lines/output_bytes/output_tail keys: it is a plain, non-quiet check, and --quiet has never actually been invoked on a real project-level check in this ticket's journal, only in the isolated unit tests at records 19-20.
findings.failure_scenario: A later reader trusting the Outcome would believe the quiet flag has already been exercised in production and search record 22 for a quiet payload shape that is not there; the 1,272-byte figure is simply record 22's already-small full output (its regression command used pytest's own -q flag), not evidence of --quiet's savings.
findings.resolution: Half right, and both halves are recorded. The figure was wrong and is corrected: 1,272 bytes is the size of the output the journal stored, not what came back to the caller, and what came back was the last 17 lines, which on that run was the whole thing. The saving at record 22 was nil, because the command already carried pytest's own -q and 17 lines is under the 20 the tail keeps. The Outcome now says that, and says the flag earns its keep on a verbose or failing run rather than on this one. The other half of the finding is mistaken and the Outcome now says so too: record 22 was run with --quiet. Its journal record holds the output in full and carries no output_omitted because that is criterion 4 working, not the flag failing to fire, and the caller's payload is the only place the flag is ever visible. Reading the journal as evidence that the flag was never passed is exactly the confusion the flag's help text exists to prevent, which is worth having on the record.
